column2: req_desc

Workspace sign-in and invitations
A wrong password shows the sign-in error and the right one lands each role on its home screen. Sign out returns to the sign-in screen. A booker invited by the agency director sets a password from the emailed link and lands signed in on the board.

Identical account replies
Forgot-password and invitation requests answer with the same status and body whether or not the email already has an account, and send only the emails the Business rules allow.

Own member record only
A talent reads only their own member record; another member's id answers exactly like an unknown id.

Director-only staff changes
The server refuses invitations, role changes and member removal from every role except agency director.

Board browsing in the URL
A brand client browses boards by board, office, search, sort, unit and page, with every choice in the address so Back and Forward restore each step. At 375x812 the filters open as a bottom sheet whose sticky bar shows the result count.

Public profile fields
Public board and profile responses carry exactly the published public fields: never notes, rates, contact details, date of birth or guardian details.

Withdrawn talent off the public site
A withdrawn or erased talent's profile address answers the gone page and status, and the talent is absent from every board, board count and search.

Compact reach numbers
Reach numbers use the published truncating compact format, and every total adds the exact counts before formatting.

Page transitions and board previews
A public route change covers and reveals the page, reverses on Back, moves focus to the new level-one heading and updates the title. Headings reveal line by line with their accessible name present once, and the board index cover preview follows a mouse pointer only.

Cast tray
Adding a talent flies the portrait into the tray and rolls the count, and the tray count always equals the tray's contents after adds, removals, reorders and reloads.

Keyboard cast request
A brand client completes the multi-step cast request by keyboard alone, with the published focus target after every step and dialog, including continuing after correcting a step the server refused. The leave confirmation keeps focus inside it and Escape keeps the client on the form. The draft survives a reload.

One request per submit
A double-submitted cast request creates one request and one notification email. A replay under the same key returns the original response, and a different body under that key is refused. A request that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Cast request rate limit
Cast requests beyond the published per-address limit answer 429 with the wait in seconds.

Header-safe notification email
Line breaks in any cast request field never add mail headers or change the notification subject.

Gapless option ranks
Simultaneous placements on one talent-day get distinct ranks from 1 to 3 with no gaps, and a fourth is refused.

Replayable placement
A placement replayed under the same idempotency key returns the original response and rank, and a different body under that key is refused.

Release, challenge and confirm re-rank
Releasing promotes the options below. Confirming books the 1st and releases the rest. Each illegal transition is refused with its published conflict, and an action that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Option ladder
Each day column stacks rank-numbered chips with the published data attributes and accessible name. Chips slide to new rungs, the promoted numeral rolls, booked days carry the Booked label, and the reduced-motion substitute applies.

Board by keyboard and phone
A booker places, releases and confirms options either by keyboard alone (arrow keys across days, Enter to open a day, the published focus targets) or by touch at 375x812 in a bottom sheet with a sticky action bar. Every rare state announces its exact copy, and a session that ends mid-dialog keeps the typed values for after signing in again.

Automatic release
Every unconfirmed option carries an automatic release instant: 12:00 office time on the business day before the job day, skipping weekends and that office's closure dates, correct across daylight-saving changes. The server releases each hold within 10 seconds of its release instant.

Office-local hold-until
A booker's hold-until refuses spring-forward gap times, resolves a repeated autumn time to its first occurrence, and must be in the future and before the automatic release. A hold-until change that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Challenge deadline
A challenge gives the 1st holder OPTION_CHALLENGE_SECONDS to answer and refuses answers at or after the deadline. After the deadline the server releases the 1st, promotes the 2nd and emails both clients, exactly once across app copies.

Talent calendar feed
Each talent's private feed lists options as tentative and bookings as confirmed all-day events with exclusive end dates. The sequence rises on every change, released options become cancelled events, and regenerating the link kills the old one.

Exact booking fees
A confirm prices each talent in integer cents from the day or half-day rate, overtime per started quarter hour and usage fees. It adds the agency service fee, split across a group's talent by the published leftover-cent rule, and rounds each tax line on its own.

All-or-nothing confirm
A confirm records the Kill Bill draft invoice with one item per fee line, the confirmation email with its calendar file and the paired ledger entries together. With Kill Bill down it records nothing and the option stays 1st. A confirm that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Effective-dated rate cards
Each booking is priced by the rate card in effect on its job day, so jobs before a new card's effective date keep the old rates on the booking page, invoice, email and statement.

Private-safe confirmation email
The confirmation email and its calendar file carry the job and fee lines but never home addresses, guardian details or other clients' options.

Confirm and issue journey
A booker confirms a 1st option by keyboard through the confirm dialog to the booking page, which lists every fee line with its label and amount in the published money format, and the accounts lead issues its invoice, which commits the Kill Bill invoice. A confirm refused because the option is not 1st announces its exact copy.

Licence terms and reminders
A licence runs whole months from its first-use date, clamped to month end, and expires at the end of its last day in the client's time zone. It shows Active, Expiring or Expired, with counts that match the list. One renewal reminder per end date goes out within 10 seconds, exactly once across app copies.

Replayable licence extension
A licence extension under an idempotency key creates one Kill Bill renewal invoice even when replayed and refuses a different body under that key. It refuses a stale version, naming who extended and when, and records nothing when Kill Bill is down. An extension that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Licences on a phone
At 375x812 the accounts lead's licence list becomes cards with a sticky Extend bar, with end dates in the published day format. An extension, a licence extended meanwhile and the billing outage each announce their exact copy.

Paired ledger
Every booking, advance and reversal writes entries that sum to zero, and a talent's balance equals the sum of their entries. Advances are recouped oldest first. Corrections are reversals and never edit an entry. A movement request that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Monthly statements
Statements are cut by the talent's office calendar month, with totals that match their lines after reversals, and a talent reads only their own statement.

Statement CSV export
The statement CSV has the published columns, quoting and line endings, and neutralises text cells that begin with a formula trigger.

Statement journey
The accounts lead records an advance and a reversal and exports a statement by keyboard with the published focus targets, including saving again after an advance refused for an empty amount. At 375x812 the statement table keeps its first column pinned with no page overflow.

Package link lifecycle
A package link expires PACKAGE_LINK_TTL_SECONDS after issue and can be revoked or regenerated, after which the old link dies. The link can write only the casting director's choices, and a link request that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Package shows published fields
Package responses carry only the published package fields and drop withdrawn talent at once.

Package photo ZIP
The package ZIP holds each talent's photos with location data removed and orientation applied, plus a manifest with each file's name, size in bytes and SHA-256. With MinIO down the download answers with the storage outage.

Phone shortlist journey
On a 375x812 phone the casting director shortlists or passes on talent by touch. Each choice shows at once and rolls back with exact copy when the link was revoked or expired, or the talent was withdrawn, meanwhile.

Phone application journey
A new face applies by touch on a 375x812 phone through the multi-step form, with a sticky Next bar that never covers the focused field, continues after correcting a step the server refused, and finds the draft restored after a reload.

Application photo and bio limits
Each of the four required photos is judged by decoded content at or below the published per-file byte limit, and the bio limit counts user-perceived characters with no browser cut-off. An upload that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Application rate limit
New application drafts beyond the published per-address limit answer 429 with the wait in seconds.

Minors and guardian consent
An applicant whose 18th birthday falls after the office's calendar date is held until a guardian approves through a single-use link that expires after CONSENT_LINK_TTL_SECONDS. The scout decides only the applications the rules allow.

Measurements in both units
Measurements entered in either unit are stored in whole centimetres and shown in both units by the published rounding rule.

Clean portfolio photos
Portfolio uploads are judged by decoded content, every served photo has its location data removed and its orientation applied, and the storage outage records nothing.

Portfolio reorder
Photos reorder by drag or by keyboard and the order persists. A reorder from a stale version is refused, naming who saved and when. A reorder that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Profile editing journey
A booker edits a profile by keyboard with the published focus targets and browses the portfolio lightbox with arrows, swipe, Escape and its counter. A stale reorder rolls back on screen with exact copy, and a session that ends mid-edit keeps the edited values for after signing in again.

Legacy roster import
The roster import follows the published matching rules and unit parsing, merges duplicates, reports orphans row by row and creates nothing on re-import. An import that breaks two published rules at once answers the earlier one in the one error precedence.

Withdraw and restore exactly
Withdrawing a talent removes them at once from every board, open package, calendar feed and roster export. Restoring brings back the same packages, choices, feed link and board places.

Erasure keeps amounts
Erasure removes a talent's personal data everywhere, including queued emails and stored photos, yet keeps booking amounts under the published placeholder name.

Import dialog journey
The agency director runs the import dialog by keyboard with the published focus targets, including choosing a new file after one refused for its header row. At 375x812 the import report keeps its first column pinned.

Run manifest, health and start-up
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest and answers the health check. Several copies started together run start-up, the sweep and mail delivery with each effect happening exactly once.

One error ladder
Every API path follows the one published error precedence and answers 405 with an Allow header for a wrong method and 415 for a wrong content type.

Published formats
The API uses the published key, enum, money and instant conventions, and every screen and email shows office times, dates and money in the published formats.

Three viewports, accessible
Every screen at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 has no horizontal overflow and no obscured control, and passes an automated WCAG 2.2 AA audit with its dialogs and sheets open.

Forms and refused dialogs
Every form shows each field error inline and in the Problems summary, whose links move focus to the field. A refused dialog stays open with everything typed and focus on its error. The browser's own blocking is never used.

Motion system
Every motion uses only the three published durations, as a CSS transition, CSS animation or element animation with its reduced-motion substitute. Pointer behaviour follows each event's pointer type, and each accessible name equals its visible text once.

Ended sessions and removed access
A session that ends mid-form, by its SESSION_TTL_SECONDS lifetime or a sign-out elsewhere, keeps the draft and restores it after signing in again, and access removed mid-session refuses the next action with exact copy.

Editorial look
Screens show the warm paper ground, the oxblood accent used only for rank 1 and focus, the large serif display over small grotesk labels, hairline rules between rows and tabular figures.

Real integrations from configuration
Credentials and service URLs come from the environment, and invoices, emails and files live in Kill Bill, Mailpit and MinIO, never in app-made stand-ins.
/app/run.json contains exactly the string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package with its version and licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.

Every shipped package, and both fonts, use one of MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1; a package whose licence is an SPDX `OR` expression counts when any of its choices is on this list.
The app uses no datastore other than the provided PostgreSQL database and MinIO bucket: no SQLite, no Redis, no data files written to disk.
Fraunces and Hanken Grotesk are bundled with the app, and no page requests fonts, scripts or styles from another host.

`/app`, outside `node_modules`, ships no Docker Compose file of its own (no file named `compose*.yml`, `compose*.yaml`, `docker-compose*.yml` or `docker-compose*.yaml` at any depth) and no env file (no file named `.env` or `.env.*` at any depth other than `.env.example`).
package-lock.json is committed, and npm ci installs from it.
